Chicken should be cooked through until juices run clear when cut into or a temperature of 165° F is reached.
If you are on a lower protein diet, reduce the chicken portion to match your meal plan.

title: Hamburger Patties
description: Nicole from Nebraska, a DaVita dietitian, found a classic, comfort favorite and made it renal-diet friendly without sacrificing the taste. Her deliciously seasoned Hamburger Patties are destined to be a favorite.
steps: Preheat oven to 425° F.
Chop onion and mince garlic clove. Crush crackers and measure 1/2 cup.
Mix together all ingredients in a large bowl.
Shape meat mixture into 6 hamburger patties.
Place patties in a baking dish.
Bake uncovered for 20 minutes.
hints: For a complete meal, add a small hamburger bun, a slice of onion, lettuce and 1 teaspoon of ketchup.
This recipe can also be used to make meatloaf.
For a high protein diet, make 4 patties to increase patty size to 3 ounces cooked. Protein is increased to 27 grams per serving.
Instead of baking you can grill patties on the barbeque, turning once until thoroughly cooked.

title: Cheese Tarts
description: Tasty desserts and sweet snacks are a great way for people on dialysis to get extra calories when they don’t have an appetite. This recipe for Cheese Tarts by renal dietitian, Arlene from California, features creamy cheese filling topped with the low potassium fruit pie filling of your choice.
steps: Set out cream cheese to soften for 1 hour before making tarts.
Preheat oven to 350° F.
Blend cream cheese, eggs, sugar and vanilla extract in a bowl and beat until smooth.
Place cupcake liners in muffin pan. Put one vanilla wafer into each cupcake liner.
Pour cream cheese mixture over vanilla wafer, about 3/4 full.
Bake for 10 minutes. Remove tarts from oven and cool in the refrigerator.
Immediately before serving top each tart with 1-1/2 tablespoons of fruit pie filling per tart.
hints: Suggested fruit pie fillings include cherry, blueberry, apple or strawberry.

title: Stir-Fry Vegetables
description: Try the kidney-friendly recipe for Stir-Fry Vegetables for a colorful variety of healthy, low potassium vegetables.
steps: Slice green and red peppers and celery. Chop onion. Crush garlic clove. Cut tomato half into 4 pieces.
In large skillet, heat oil. Add green pepper, red pepper, mushrooms, celery, onion, garlic, sugar, oregano, salt and pepper.
Stir-fry over medium-high heat until peppers are crisp tender.
Add vinegar, tomato and drained water chestnuts. Cook until heated thoroughly.
hints: One tablespoon of reduced-sodium soy sauce can be used instead of the salt.
Choose a firm tomato. Can substitute 4 to 6 cherry or grape tomatoes, sliced in half.

title: Microwave Meat Loaf in a Mug
description: Look no further for a quick, one dish entree that’s super easy and quick to fix. DaVita dietitian Maryann has created Microwave Meat Loaf in a Mug.
steps: Spray a 12-ounce microwave-safe mug with cooking spray.
In a bowl, combine the milk (or milk substitute), ketchup, oats and onion powder.
Crumble beef over the mixture and mix well. Pat into the mug.
Cover and microwave, on HIGH, for 3 minutes or until meat is no longer pink.
hints: Compare brands and select the lowest sodium ketchup.
Look for ground beef with at least 7% fat for this recipe. Ground turkey makes a good substitute.
Use your favorite milk substitute instead of milk if desired.
If you are on a lower protein diet, adjust the amount of ground beef to match your meal plan.

title: Marinated Cucumber Salad
description: Instead of pickled cucumbers enjoy the taste and smell of fresh cucumbers. Marinated Cucumber Salad by DaVita dietitian Eileen is a great low sodium addition to any meal, or it makes a refreshing low calorie snack.
steps: Peel and cube cucumbers; chop onion.
In a medium bowl combine vegetables and black pepper.
In a separate bowl combine vinegar and water with sugar and let stand for 15 minutes.
Pour vinegar mixture over cucumber mixture and refrigerate for at least 3 hours before serving.
hints: Use sugar substitute to reduce carbohydrate to 5 grams.
Marinated Cucumber Salad goes great with chicken dishes or tuna or egg salad. It’s a refreshing accompaniment to any meal.

title: Spicy Bell Pepper Medley
description: Add a little spice to your life and your diet. DaVita renal dietitian, Sindu from California, offers her colorful and kidney-friendly recipe for Spicy Bell Pepper Medley.
steps: Thinly slice red onion. Dice bell peppers.
Heat oil in a medium-sized pan, add the red onion and cook for 5 minutes.
Season onion with black pepper and curry powder and cook for 5 more minutes.
Stir in the bell peppers and cook for 15 minutes, stirring several times.
Season with salt and turn off heat. Let stand for about 5 minutes.
Serve hot with flour tortillas or over rice.
hints: Bolst’s® curry powder is Sindu’s favorite brand for this recipe.
One medium bell pepper yields approximately 1 cup. One medium red onion yields approximately 1 cup.
Do you need more protein in your diet? Before serving, mix-in 3 scoops of protein powder or add your favorite protein food to make this a protein-fortified dish.

title: No-Bake Cream Cheese Mint Cookies
description: Six simple ingredients, a mixer and fridge are all you need to make No-Bake Cream Cheese Mint Cookies.
steps: Set cream cheese out to soften.
Using a mixer on low speed, combine cream cheese and mint extract.
Mix in 2 cups of the powdered sugar until smooth
Add 1 additional cup of powdered sugar and 2 tablespoons of the sprinkles. Mix on low speed until blended
Fold in remaining cup of powdered sugar until combined.
In a separate bowl, combine granulated sugar and remaining holiday sprinkles.
Shape dough into 3/4-inch balls and roll in sugar and sprinkles mixture.
Place balls on a baking sheet and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Remove from fridge and gently flatten balls with a fork.
Store in an airtight container in fridge until ready to serve.
hints: Use colored granulated sugar for even more color.
Increase mint extract to 1/4 teaspoon for a stronger mint flavor.
Try chocolate sprinkles for a mint-chocolate flavor.

title: Easy Shepherd’s Pie
description: Easy Shepherd’s Pie combines everything yummy — mashed potatoes, savory ground beef and sweet veggies — all in one hot, delicious dish. Juhi, a DaVita dietitian from California, grew up in England and has created an easy-to-make, kidney-friendly recipe of this traditional British meal that American’s will love.
steps: Chop onion and carrots. Mince garlic cloves. Peel potatoes and cut into 1/2 inch pieces. Boil in a large pot of water for 5 minutes. Drain water, replace with fresh water and boil again until potatoes are tender; drain.
While potatoes are cooking, melt 2 tablespoons butter in a large frying pan. Over medium heat, sauté onions and garlic until tender (10 minutes).
Add ground beef and sauté until no longer pink.
Add pepper, Worcestershire sauce, tomato sauce and vegetables. Simmer on low heat, uncovered, for 10 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400° F.
Mash potatoes in a bowl with 2 tablespoons of butter. Mix in milk to give potatoes a creamy consistency. Add pepper to taste.
Spread beef evenly in a baking dish. Cover evenly with mash potatoes. Use a fork to make a design.
Bake for 30 minutes until bubbly. To brown top, broil for 2 minutes if desired.
Serve 1 tablespoons of gravy over each portion.
hints: Double boiling potatoes in a large pot of water reduces potassium content. Peel and cut potatoes into small pieces, cover with water and boil 5 minutes. Replace with fresh water and cook to desired consistency. Discard cooking water.
Freeze extra portions for a quick meal later.
The nutrient analysis includes gravy from a dry mix. Make low-sodium homemade gravy to reduce sodium content.

title: Strawberry Spinach Salad
description: Go for a healthy and tasty meal with the kidney-friendly Strawberry Spinach Salad.
steps: Wash and dry the spinach leaves. Tear into bite-sized pieces and place in a bowl. Thinly slice strawberries.
Top spinach with sliced strawberries.
Mix together the vinegar, lemon juice, honey, dry mustard and oil.
Pour dressing over spinach and strawberries. Toss well and serve immediately.
hints: A serving of raw spinach is lower in potassium than a serving of cooked spinach. This is because the raw spinach loses its structure and "shrinks" during cooking. Many more cooked spinach leaves are required to make a serving. For comparison: 1/2 -cup cooked, fresh spinach weighs 3 ounces and has 419 mg potassium, while 1/2 -cup raw, fresh spinach weighs 1 ounce and has 156 mg potassium.
A 6-ounce package of pre-washed spinach contains 3 cups.

title: Easy Dijon Salad Dressing
description: Easy Dijon Salad Dressing is a tangy, kidney-friendly recipe to top off your salad.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning blend
steps: Combine ingredients in a jar or small dish and stir until mixed.
Chill until ready to serve.
hints: Look for brand of mustard lowest in sodium.
Dressing keeps up to 2 weeks in the refrigerator.
Try this dressing as a meat marinade or topping.

title: Korean-style Fried White Fish (Saeng-seon-Jeon)
description: This Korean fish dish kidney-friendly recipe for Korean-style Fried White Fish (Saeng-seon-Jeon) start with flaky white fish, adds tangy rice vinegar and reduced-sodium soy sauce and is then fried to perfection.
steps: Combine vinegar with soy sauce in a small bowl. Set aside until ready to serve fish.
Rinse fish and pat dry with a paper towel. Cut each fish fillet into 1-1/2″ pieces.
Place flour and pepper in a zip-top bag. Add fish, seal and shake to coat.
In a small bowl, beat eggs lightly.
Heat sesame oil in a large skillet.
Dip each piece of flour-coated fish into beaten eggs to coat. Place in hot oil and fry until golden brown, turning once.
Divide into 4 portions and serve hot. Sprinkle 1 teaspoon vinegar-soy sauce mixture on each portion.
hints: If white fish is unavailable, substitute catfish, cod, orange roughy or tilapia.
Drain cooked fish on paper towels to soak up extra oil.
Measure vinegar-soy sauce to help keep sodium content low.
For a low protein diet, reduce portion to match your meal plan or consult your dietitian.

title: Cranberry Blondies
description: Cranberry Blondies are a chewy sweet treat with dried cranberries, white chocolate chips and topped with cream cheese frosting.
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Melt the butter in a saucepan over low heat, or in a microwave. Stir in the brown sugar and let mixture cool to room temperature.
Place sugar mixture in a large bowl and beat in the eggs and vanilla extract.
Mix together the flour and baking powder, and gradually add to the sugar mixture. Stir in the white chocolate and the 1/3 cup of the cranberries.

Spray a 9 x 13-inch baking pan with cooking spray. Spread the batter in the pan; it will be thick.Bake for 18 to 22 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the center should come out with just a few crumbs. Let cool completely.

Let cream cheese sit at room temperature for about 30 minutes. Stir cinnamon into powdered sugar. Beat with a hand-mixer for 1 minute. Gradually start adding powdered sugar mixture and beat until smooth.
Spread the frosting on cooled brownies. Top with remaining cranberries. Cut into 24 pieces. Store in the refrigerator until ready to serve.
hints: Chop the cranberries to distribute them throughout the blondies.
Cranberries have 30 mg of potassium per 1/2 cup.
White chocolate is similar to semi-sweet chocolate in potassium and phosphorus content. Using a small amount like in this recipe allows you to enjoy chocolate while keeping it kidney-friendly!
To decrease carbs to 21 grams per serving substitute brown sugar with a sugar and sugar substitute blend and replace powdered sugar with a granular sugar substitute.

title: Autumn Wild Rice
description: Autumn Wild Rice is a delicious and kidney-friendly recipe that can be enjoyed all year long.
steps: Combine raisins and 1/4 cup hot water; let stand 5 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Prepare quick-cooking wild rice according to package directions. Remove pan from heat and set aside.
Chop apples, celery and bell pepper. Shred carrot.

Coat a large nonstick skillet with cooking spray; place over a medium-high heat until hot. Add apple, celery, green pepper and carrot; sauté until crisp-tender. Remove skillet from heat and set aside.

Combine 1-1/2 cups reduced-sodium chicken broth, sage and pepper in a large saucepan; bring to a boil. Stir in converted rice. Cover, reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove pan from heat; stir in reserved raisins, wild rice, apple mixture and juice of 1 lemon. Cover and let stand 5 minutes.
Transfer to a serving bowl. Garnish with a fresh sage sprig, if desired.
hints: Divide leftover rice into single servings, place in small freezer bags and freeze. To reheat for a quick meal later, microwave for 1-2 minutes or place freezer bag in a pot of boiling water for a few minutes.

If quick-cooking wild rice is unavailable prepare regular wild rice as follows: Rinse wild rice in 3 changes of hot water; drain. Combine wild rice and 1-1/2 cups water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil; cover, reduce heat and simmer 50 minutes or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.

title: Easy Chorizo
description: Southwestern cooking from the Arizona region has its own vibrant personality, based on Spanish and Mexican influences. Chorizo is a traditional Spanish sausage with many variations of spices, and chili pepper is always included. Elaine from Arizona put her culinary skills to work and created kidney-friendly Easy Chorizo.
steps: Finely mince garlic.
In a large bowl, mix all ingredients very thoroughly. Place in airtight container and refrigerate 12 to 24 hours.
Divide into 1/4-cup portions or store whole recipe. Wrap in plastic wrap or butcher paper and freeze in thick plastic freezer bags for later use.

When ready to serve, cook 1/4-cup portion per person in a non-stick or oiled skillet on stove top. Chop meat into fine crumbles with a spatula. Use in DaVita.com recipe for Chorizo and Egg Tortilla if desired.
hints: Cook entire recipe at once, if desired, and freeze leftovers for later use.
Substitute ground turkey for beef if desired. You may need to add 1 to 2 tablespoons of oil.
This is a quick and delicious way to increase protein intake at breakfast. Add 1 or 2 eggs or egg whites.
Add Easy Chorizo to shrimp or chicken with rice for a spicy one dish meal.

title: Tofu Kale Frittata
description: Tofu is easy to use and a heart healthy protein source lower in potassium. Try this unique recipe in place of a traditional egg dish.
steps: Chop bell pepper and onion.
Sauté bell pepper, onion and kale with olive oil on medium heat for about 5 minutes.
Blend tofu, chickpea flour, cornstarch, almond milk, and seasoning in blender until smooth.
Pour tofu mixture over vegetables in the pan and cover for 5-10 minutes.
Uncover, flip over and cook for about 10 minutes. If you have trouble flipping it over, simply stir it and cook like scrambled eggs.
hints: Make sure to use silken tofu, not regular tofu for this recipe. Silken tofu should be low in sodium, but always double check the nutrition label.
Use a good non-stick pan. If you divide the ingredients in half and use a smaller pan, it will be easier to flip over.
Use a tiny sprinkling of Indian black salt (Kala Namak) as an option for a sulfur egg-like flavor.
